## Intent
Separate maintenance from work: work is immutable, maintenance is not (owner ruling 2026-07-14).

What an intent DELIVERED (intent text, spec, plan, outcome) is frozen once terminal and must never be
edited so the intent looks like it delivered something else. But MAINTENANCE (structural consistency:
closing an intent, making structure uniform across stores, reprojecting Links, moving a section where
it belongs) is explicitly allowed on terminal intents, on one condition: every fix is recorded in the
intent's `revisions.md` and runs through a Plastic maintenance skill, never a hand edit.

PLASTIC.md must state the distinction plainly so no agent confuses the two, because today's blanket
terminal-immutability rule DEADLOCKS the store: a real structural defect cannot be repaired for the
sole reason that the intent is Completed. That is exactly how the three `graph_links_projection`
violations (global 26, dealintell 3b, dealintell 15) survived the two intents built to fix them: 189
and 192 both closed with the repair PROPOSED, not run.

Second half: doctor must CATCH the defect, not merely offer to fix it. A hand-authored `## Links` line
with a malformed slug (dealintell 3b points at `3d-payments-subscription-gating`, one dash, while the
real directory is `3d--payments-subscription-gating`) resolves nowhere, so it is invisible to 192's
write-time Links gate AND to 189's preserve-rule, which only preserves an unbacked line that RESOLVES.
A broken link is therefore silently droppable and nobody is ever told.

Verified 2026-07-14: those three 3b lines are genuinely junk and SHOULD drop (3c, 3d and 3e are
siblings all sourced from 3, so a chain edge from 3b would be a FALSE edge, and the three seams are
already stated in 3b's own Context prose), while 15's line is real and the frontmatter is what is
missing, so the edge belongs on `3a.chain`. Reprojection destroys nothing. The bug is the SILENCE, not
the deletion.

Deliverables: a malformed-ref scan in doctor, plus a check that maintenance was recorded in
`revisions.md`; repair of the three live violations THROUGH the new maintenance path as the proof case,
never by hand; and a ruling on the 44 `signals_complete` terminal gaps (40 missing `outcome.md`, 3
missing the savepoint `Done` echo, 1 placeholder). The `Done` echo is mechanical and is plain
maintenance. A missing `outcome.md` is a delivery CLAIM that maintenance must not invent, so the choice
is between a frozen amnesty allowlist (precedent 170a) and an honest reconstructed stub.

2026-07-16T09:10:07Z · why · human — OWNER RULING 2026-07-16 (when maintenance needs an intent + the data-backfill stance). (1) Maintenance normally needs NO intent and NO roadmap - it runs through the maintenance skills and records itself in revisions.md. (2) EXCEPTION - maintenance needs an intent + a roadmap ONLY when it is a batch of many different things at once (rule of thumb: more than ~5 intents to fix or add something to). This must be RARE. (3) Data-backfill stance: stay away from backfilling DONE intents. Only Future and Active intents should undergo backfills as normal work. (4) EXCEPTION to (3): if a DONE (past) intent is missing a KEY thing for Plastic OPERATIONS - e.g. an operational file is missing so the intent cannot be read/processed - then fix it via maintenance + revisions.md as already implemented. Cosmetic or delivery-claim gaps in Done intents are NOT operational and do not qualify. (5) Any such backfill batch is an owner decision: the agent must ALWAYS ask first and ALWAYS present what changes in the batch and what the difference is (the diff), and proceed only after the owner allows it.
2026-07-16T09:10:07Z · why · human — OWNER RULINGS 2026-07-16 on A-D. C (settled): NO maintenance lock is needed; revisions.md captures the change diff itself (removals, additions, modifications - every destructive or modifying action). Drop the second-lock model; the delivery lock stays as the only lock and the revisions.md receipt is the whole maintenance contract. This matches parked intent 122's own conclusion. B (settled direction): doctor stays a DETECTOR (core + full, all installed agents, global + project stores); it does NOT gain a write mode. A doctor --fix-all is a ROUTER that dispatches each detected exception to the appropriate maintenance skill/agent, and THOSE skills do the writing and record revisions.md. 'read vs write on doctor' was the wrong framing - doctor detects and routes, the skills mutate.
2026-07-16T10:49:15Z · why · human — OWNER RULING 2026-07-16 (A, refined - the precise immutability line). WORK is immutable: work done by a DONE intent cannot be changed except through ANOTHER intent that continues or reverts that work. Changing a Done intent's artifacts so it looks like the intent performed or delivered something else is FORBIDDEN - that axis is immutable. BUT structural fixes to core files are NOT that: if a file contains a section it should not, or the structure needs a fix (Links repair, frontmatter formatting), that goes through the MAINTENANCE mechanisms (revisions.md receipt), not through a new intent and not by hand. So the test is WHAT changes: delivery-meaning = immutable, needs a continue/revert intent; structure/format = maintenance.

Reason: it does not scale past this one user - it defines fixes for MY store, not for all users. FINDING (verified 2026-07-16): scripts/lib/legacy_bookend_amnesty.rb ALREADY ships in the npm package (scripts/ is in package.json files array; npm pack --dry-run confirms the file is packed) and it hardcodes the OWNER's personal intent ids (global: 1a,1a2,23; project:plastic: ~70 ids). Every Plastic installer worldwide receives one user's intent numbers baked into shipped maintenance code. This is the exact anti-pattern the owner flagged. What Plastic must instead define is the BARE MINIMUM set of fixes that apply to ALL users generically (rules, not id lists). DECISION: leave the 44 signals_complete gaps alone for now; do NOT amnesty them; spin the whole old-intent-maintenance question into a NEW intent. Also: the shipped amnesty file is itself a defect to address in that new intent (a store-specific id list must not ship in the package).

Direction right, do not ship the PLASTIC.md prose until the mechanical layer lands, or it rots exactly like the abandoned 112 gate. Three load-bearing changes: (1) ENFORCEMENT: a prose-only 'must record revisions.md' rule is unenforceable and doctor CANNOT enforce it (doctor sees the store at rest; a clean maintenance write leaves no at-rest residue). Put the floor in the four MUTATING tools: project-links/rebuild-graph/restore-intent-v1/curator must write revisions.md in the SAME write as the change or abort. restore_intent_v1.rb already does exactly this for frontmatter; generalize that one pattern. This must be a named deliverable in the ACs - today it is only assumed, which is the whole thesis left implicit. (2) THE DISTINCTION 'meaning vs structure' is NOT decidable: the 15/3a proof-case repair ADDS a frontmatter sources/chain edge, which is BOTH structure AND a delivered-lineage claim; two honest agents split on it. Re-key the test from meaning to FIELD TOUCHED: FREE maintenance (records revisions.md, no ask) = Links-body projection, formatting, section move, uniformity (things with a mechanical source of truth); OWNER-DIFF maintenance (always ask + show diff) = frontmatter sources/chain edges and delivery-claim sections. 26 and 3b are clean free-maintenance; only 15/3a is boundary and the spec already gates it behind owner approval - generalize that into the rule. (3) NO-LOCK HAS A HOLE: dropping the second lock TYPE is fine, but the surviving delivery lock does NOT reach terminal intents (bridge.rb:1195 ALLOWs all terminal writes), so there is ZERO mutual exclusion on a terminal intent - two maintenance sessions, or a maintenance write racing the end-intent delivery-tail (intent is terminal but tail still writing), are un-arbitrated; store auto-commit is git add -A so a concurrent commit can land a change WITHOUT its receipt. Mitigate: write change+receipt in one transaction and commit SCOPED paths (git add <paths>), not add -A. Rival B held behind a kill trigger: if a race is ever seen, reuse the ONE delivery lock to arbitrate terminal writes (a hand Edit holds no lock so it is denied - also enforces 'through a skill'). SCOPE: the malformed-ref scan is largely REDUNDANT (graph_links_projection already flags all 3); the REAL uncovered bug is project-links SILENTLY DROPPING unresolvable Links lines - fix = report them as orphan candidates instead of dropping, same as it already does for resolvable orphans. KILL CRITERION: at plan/exec, require naming the exact code change that makes project-links (or a named substitute) write the receipt for the 3 repairs WITHOUT a hand edit; if the only path is a manual edit + hand-written revisions.md, STOP - the intent has disproven itself.
2026-07-16T12:10:24Z · why · human — OWNER CORRECTION 2026-07-16 - OVERRIDES the advisor's Hole 2 classification. The immutable axis is NOT the frontmatter graph. Delivery/WORK = using an intent's artifacts to change CODE + project files (dealintell: code in the repo), record research, etc. - the DELIVERED CONTENT. Modifying an intent's artifacts does NOT change the code, so editing artifacts to make a Done intent look like it delivered something different or that feature parts are missing is FORBIDDEN (book analogy: never change the text written on the pages of an old, valuable book). sources/chain edges and structure are metadata/relationships, NOT delivery meaning - fixing them is legitimate MAINTENANCE with a revisions.md record (book analogy: reorder dropped pages, fix the cover; if a page has a defect you may fix it BUT record the revision). So the advisor's 'frontmatter sources/chain edges always need owner approval' is WRONG: fixing a wrong/dangling/missing graph edge is ordinary structural maintenance with a record. Allowed maintenance = (a) frontmatter chain/sources that points to a non-existent or wrong intent, or a missing required edge; (b) an extra non-convention section in the intent file - remove it and move it into revisions.md; (c) a new Plastic version's operational change that must apply to ALL intents in a store (e.g. add/remove a frontmatter field) - ensure every intent has it (owner muses a local DB would help; not yet); (d) any other structural/operational tidy. Forbidden = anything that alters what the work DELIVERED. The dealintell 15/3a repair is therefore ordinary maintenance (add the missing 3a.chain += 15 edge with a record), NOT an owner-gated exception. Real precedent found: plastic 124's revisions.md v1 removed a chain edge to a non-existent 124b [rule: broken-chain] and v2 added a missing required reciprocity edge to 131 - exactly this class.
2026-07-16T12:10:24Z · why · human — OWNER RULINGS 2026-07-16 - Hole 1 + Hole 3 mechanics. HOLE 1: revisions.md is APPEND-ONLY - if it exists you append a new ## Revision vN, never overwrite. Real precedent: plastic 124 revisions.md v3 corrects a false statement in v2 by APPENDING a correction entry and explicitly leaving v2 in place ('this file is append-only'). revisions.md lives IN the target intent's own directory (co-located where the change happened), never as a central/directional index. HOLE 3: never 'git add -A' anywhere - a session commits ONLY the files it changed, in BOTH the store and the project repo, by explicit path. The stronger structural guarantee is ISOLATION: a session working in its OWN git worktree + branch cannot be clobbered by another session's add -A, because add -A only stages that worktree's copy - this is exactly intent 178 (store worktrees: wire in or retire; provisioned today but agents never use them, and the store auto-commit still does add -A at the store root). 'Change + its revisions.md written as one transaction' is achieved through git, not filesystem magic: write both files then a SINGLE scoped commit staging the change AND its revisions.md together; the commit is the atomic unit; if the process dies before commit you have an uncommitted change-without-record in the working tree that is detectable and never committed as a lie; worktree isolation stops any other session's commit from sweeping up the half-done state. So the mechanism = per-session store worktree+branch (178) + scoped commit of change+record together. NOTE: 'rule's receipt' was sloppy wording by the agent - it means the revisions.md record; dropped.
2026-07-16T12:37:47Z · why · human — OWNER RULING 2026-07-16 - maintenance target states + wait-on-delivery. Maintenance is allowed on FUTURE intents as well as terminal (Done/Abandoned) ones - it is NOT limited to finished intents. The ONE thing maintenance must respect: if the target intent is ACTIVE and mid-delivery, maintenance WAITS for that delivery to finish before modifying anything (never edit an intent while its delivery is in flight). Mechanically this reuses the single delivery lock as the coordination signal (no second lock): if the target holds a live delivery lock, maintenance defers and reports, exactly as merged-in intent 122 proposed ('skipping and reporting any intent that holds a live delivery lock'). So the maintenance-eligibility rule is: Future = yes; Terminal = yes; Active-and-being-delivered = wait until delivery completes. Every maintenance change still carries its append-only revisions.md record regardless of the target's state.

2026-07-16T13:17:22Z · why · human — OWNER RULING 2026-07-16 - maintenance DETECTS the lock, NEVER acquires it (OVERRIDES advisor Ruling-4c). There is exactly ONE lock: the delivery lock, and it means 'an active agent is delivering this intent'. Maintenance must NOT acquire any lock, because a maintenance-held lock could be mistaken by a resuming/continuation session for an active delivery lock. So maintenance is DETECT-ONLY: if the target holds a FRESH delivery lock (active delivery in progress) maintenance defers and reports; otherwise it proceeds. Maintenance leaves NO lock behind, so there is nothing to clean up at the end of maintenance and no ambiguity - 'one lock' literally means only the active delivery agent ever holds a lock. A STALE lock is NOT maintenance's problem to resolve (that belongs to delivery/continuation/reclaim); maintenance simply treats not-fresh as not-active. The advisor's 'acquire the lock transiently' is rejected on this ground. The residual maintenance-vs-maintenance concurrency is handled by the branch-and-merge model (next ruling), not by locking.
2026-07-16T13:17:22Z · why · human — OWNER RULING 2026-07-16 - stranding avoided by branch-and-merge, not heavy worktrees. Maintenance does NOT need worktrees. Mechanism: create a NEW branch from the CURRENT state of store main, apply ONLY maintenance's own scoped changes (exclude anything maintenance never touched), then MERGE that branch back to main as part of the same closed operation. Because merge-back is part of the op, nothing strands (the advisor's silent-stranding risk is designed out). Because it is a fresh branch off current main with only maintenance's paths, it does not clobber concurrent work; two concurrent maintenance runs reconcile as merge conflicts on main, never silent loss. Owner preference: if the stranding/clobber problem can be avoided ALTOGETHER by construction, that is best. Every maintenance change still carries its append-only revisions.md record. This is lighter than intent 178's full agent-write-path worktrees (178 stays about delivery write paths); maintenance just needs branch-from-main + scoped-merge-back.
